io.inputs_and_states: Liquid dispersions of nanoparticles, polymers or proteins in compatible optical-bottom microplates. Select wells, plate format, acquisition duration, replicates, laser power and temperature in DYNAMICS Touch. Enter solvent properties and concentration/calibration information for the intended analysis. Electrical power and Ethernet support acquisition. Low-temperature operation may require the documented dry-gas purge.
io.outputs_and_states: DLS correlation data, hydrodynamic-radius distributions and polydispersity. SLS molar mass and particle-concentration analysis require suitable sample and concentration/calibration information. Well images, temperature records and exported results. The liquid sample remains in the plate.
io.units_of_measure: nm (hydrodynamic radius 0.5–1000 nm), Da or MDa (SLS molar mass 300 Da–1 MDa), °C (4–85 °C), µL (sample volume), s (1–3600 s acquisition), mg/mL (concentration), % (laser power 10–100).

io.inputs_and_states: Liquid nanoparticle or macromolecule dispersion in a supported cuvette. Enter solvent viscosity/refractive index, concentration and analysis method. Set acquisition time, laser power, temperature or temperature ramp using DYNAMICS Touch. Supply electrical power and the documented computer connection. Appropriate cells and purge conditions are required at temperature extremes.
io.outputs_and_states: DLS hydrodynamic-radius distributions and polydispersity. SLS molar mass, size-dependent particle concentration and turbidity under the documented analysis conditions. Correlation functions and temperature-dependent measurements. Sample remains in the cuvette.
io.units_of_measure: nm (hydrodynamic radius 0.2–1000 nm), Da or MDa (300 Da–10 MDa), particles/mL (size dependent), NTU (turbidity), µL (sample volume), °C (−10 to 120 °C), °C/min (ramp), s (acquisition).

io.inputs_and_states: Liquid particle or macromolecule dispersion in a DLS cuvette, ELS cell or supported flow cell. Supply solvent properties and sample concentration as needed. Select optical mode, temperature, acquisition time and laser power in DYNAMICS Touch. ELS additionally uses the cell electrodes and applied field. Ethernet, USB, Auto Inject contact closure and two ±10 V analog inputs are documented.
io.outputs_and_states: DLS hydrodynamic-radius distributions and polydispersity. SLS molar mass, turbidity and size-dependent particle concentration. ELS electrophoretic mobility and derived zeta potential with conductivity. Optical signals and acquisition records. Sample remains in the cell or leaves through the flow outlet.
io.units_of_measure: nm or µm (hydrodynamic radius 0.2–1000 nm in cuvette, up to 400 nm in flow cell), mV (zeta potential), mS/cm (conductivity 0–250), Da or MDa (molar mass), particles/mL, NTU, °C (mode dependent), s, V (analog inputs).

io.inputs_and_states: Liquid lipid-nanoparticle or other compatible dispersion in a Stunner plate. Load standards, untreated samples and assay reagents such as RiboGreen for the selected fluorescence assay. Select UV/Vis, rotating-angle DLS, SLS and fluorescence measurements. Windows 11 computer, USB and 100–240 V AC at 50–60 Hz support operation.
io.outputs_and_states: Hydrodynamic diameter, polydispersity and aggregate peaks. UV/Vis payload concentration, particle concentration from the configured light-scattering analysis and fluorescence-based free-RNA data. Encapsulation efficiency is calculated using the validated assay and controls. Exported spectra and sample results.
io.units_of_measure: nm (hydrodynamic diameter 0.3–1000 nm), particles/mL, % (encapsulation efficiency and peak fractions), µg/mL or ng/µL (payload), mg/mL (protein), OD (absorbance), nm (wavelength), µL (sample volume), s or min (acquisition).

io.inputs_and_states: Liquid nanoparticle or polymer dispersion in a supported cell, with solvent viscosity, refractive index, temperature and concentration information for the chosen analysis. Set detector angle, acquisition and polarization. The modular system requires a configured laser, detector and correlator. An external circulator controls the sample bath. Current TurboCorr configuration communicates by USB.
io.outputs_and_states: Dynamic light-scattering correlation functions, diffusion/particle-size analysis and size distributions. Static light-scattering intensity versus angle/concentration supports molecular weight, radius of gyration and virial analysis with appropriate calibration. Sample remains in the cell. Available analyses depend on the correlator/software configuration.
io.units_of_measure: ° (scattering angle), nm (particle size or radius of gyration, quantity specified by analysis), °C (sample temperature), s or ns (correlation delay), g/mol (molar mass), mg/mL (sample concentration), nm (laser wavelength).

io.inputs_and_states: Particle or macromolecule solution flowing from a compatible SEC/FFF separation or a supported batch accessory. Supply solvent refractive index, concentration-detector data and dn/dc for absolute molar-mass analysis. Set laser, temperature option and acquisition in ASTRA. Ethernet, four ±10 V analog inputs and Auto Inject/Alarm/Recycle signals support instrument coordination.
io.outputs_and_states: Angular scattering intensities and derived molar mass and radius of gyration under the selected model. Analog signals, acquisition triggers, alarms and Ethernet results. Liquid eluate exits the flow cell. Hydrodynamic radius is available only with the optional DLS hardware.
io.units_of_measure: Da or g/mol (molar mass, 200 Da–1 GDa), nm (radius of gyration, approximately 10–500 nm), °C (configuration dependent), V (±10 V analog I/O), nm (658 nm laser, 785 nm option), % (laser power), mL/min (connected system flow).

io.inputs_and_states: Aqueous or organic nanoparticle/macromolecule eluate from a compatible FFF or SEC system. Provide concentration and refractive-index increment for molar-mass calculation. Set laser power, detector processing and temperature. Supply 100–240 V, 50–60 Hz and an Ethernet-connected PC. Error and Injection Ready inputs coordinate acquisition.
io.outputs_and_states: 21-angle light-scattering intensities, molar mass and radius of gyration using the selected analysis and concentration data. Detector signals, Error/Injection Ready outputs and Ethernet records. Eluate exits the vertical flow cell. Vapor and leak sensors monitor faults.
io.units_of_measure: Da (sample-dependent molar mass 200–10^12 Da), nm (radius of gyration approximately 8–500 nm), ° (angles), µL (cell volume), bar (pressure limit 5 bar), °C (cell temperature), nm (532 nm laser), mW (2.5–50 mW laser), V (signal).

io.inputs_and_states: Liquid dispersion with compatible carrier solvent, channel membrane and spacer. A configured HPLC pump and injection system deliver the sample. Set cross-flow/focusing/elution sequence and detector flow in VISION. Electrical power and Ethernet support control. Optional mobility hardware additionally applies a field and measures pH/conductivity.
io.outputs_and_states: Size-fractionated liquid eluate delivered to downstream detectors or the fraction-collection port, plus membrane permeate/waste. Flow, pressure and sequence records, Alarm Out and auxiliary signal acquisition. Particle mass/size measurements require the appropriate downstream detector and analysis.
io.units_of_measure: mL/min (cross-flow 0.03–6.67), bar (channel pressure), °C (channel temperature), µm (250–1000 µm spacer options), kDa (membrane cutoff), min or s (method time). V, mA and pH apply to the optional mobility module.

io.inputs_and_states: Liquid particle/polymer/protein dispersion, carrier liquid and compatible AF4 membrane/channel. Select injection amount, focusing, channel flow and cross-flow program in NovaFFF. Manual valve or PN5300 autosampler loads the sample. Supply electrical power and the documented PC/control interface. AT and MT configurations have different temperature capabilities.
io.outputs_and_states: Size-fractionated eluate for configured UV, RI, light-scattering or other detectors, plus membrane permeate/waste. Flow-method and retention records. NovaFFF analysis can derive size using FFF theory/calibration when the required data are supplied. Absolute optical mass/size outputs require configured detectors.
io.units_of_measure: µL (injection), µg (injected mass), mL (channel volume), µL/min or mL/min (cross-flow 6.25 µL/min–7.5 mL/min), mL/min (channel flow 0–10), bar (0–35), nm or µm (separation size), kDa (membrane cutoff), min (method time).

io.inputs_and_states: Liquid chromatographic/FFF eluate and compatible reference/mobile phase. Enter dn/dc to convert differential refractive index into concentration, or use known concentrations for dn/dc determination. Set temperature, response time, zero and purge controls. Ethernet, ±10 V Analog In and contact signals coordinate acquisition.
io.outputs_and_states: Differential and absolute refractive-index signals. Concentration or dn/dc results require the corresponding supplied constants/known concentrations. Liquid eluate, digital data, selectable analog signal and Auto Inject/Alarm/Recycle outputs. Vapor/leak fault monitoring.
io.units_of_measure: RIU (differential refractive index, standard range −0.0047 to +0.0047), RIU (absolute index 1.2–1.8), °C (4–65 °C), s (0.1–5 response), Hz (10 Hz digital output), V (analog signals), psi or bar (back pressure), µL (fill volume).

io.inputs_and_states: Liquid nanoparticle dispersion with suitable concentration and solvent viscosity information. Load the flow cell/syringe and select temperature, capture and analysis conditions in NS Xplorer. Installed laser and fluorescence filters determine detection mode. Electrical power, computer and USB-3 camera support acquisition.
io.outputs_and_states: Videos and individual particle tracks, number-based hydrodynamic-diameter distributions and particle concentration. Fluorescence-resolved subpopulations require the installed fluorescence configuration. Acquisition/analysis reports and liquid effluent from the cell. No zeta-potential output is assigned.
io.units_of_measure: nm (hydrodynamic diameter 10–1000 nm, sample dependent), particles/mL (10^6–10^9), µL (minimum sample 250), °C (10 °C below ambient to 70 °C), nm (installed laser 405/488/532/642), s (capture time), mL (syringe volume).

purdue_review.result: No exact-model Purdue installation was independently confirmed. Existing original Purdue-list flags and documented installations are unchanged.

rejected_matches.reason: BI-200SM is reported in a multi-institution study with Purdue coauthors. The paper does not locate that instrument at Purdue.
Purdue lists Optilab T-rEX and miniDAWN TREOS. These are different models/generations from the new Optilab and DAWN records.
Purdue-hosted advertisement describes a University of Florida facility and NanoSight NS300, not a Purdue NanoSight Pro.

price_review.estimate_rule: Older official MSRP/list +20%, otherwise 120% of category minimum to 80% of maximum. No qualifying exact predecessor or valid category benchmark range was verified for the eight unpriced records.

rejected_matches.reason: NanoSight Pro fluorescence accessory, not the complete instrument.
